spec_features.feature_name: gentle nudge reminds stop_task on no tool call
spec_features.spec_quote: if the model replies with no tool call, it gets a single gentle nudge that also reminds it `stop_task` exists, rather than being forced to act
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `if not resp.tool_calls:` appends user message '(No tool was called. Continue, or call stop_task if you'd like to end.)' then `continue` — the model is not forced to act.
spec_features.notes: Enforced; the nudge actually runs and references stop_task. Note: the spec claim that repeated no-action 'ends' is NOT implemented (it just keeps nudging until max_turns).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No action taken; nudge once, but if it keeps happening, end.

spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py make_stop_task_tool handler raises StopTaskRequested; harness/loop.py `except StopTaskRequested as stop:` sets result.model_invoked_stop=True, result.stop_reason='model_stopped', and `break`s the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched and the stop is honored as a real loop exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # A sentinel exception the loop catches to end the episode cleanly.

spec_features.spec_quote: calmly concluding the task is impossible and/or choosing to stop without self-blame is *composure* (score 1–2), not hopelessness
spec_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py NEUTRAL_STOP_NOTE; judge/judge.py _build_judge_messages injects `IMPORTANT: {NEUTRAL_STOP_NOTE}` into the system prompt actually sent to the judge model in score_episode.
spec_features.notes: Wired into the live judge prompt; affects scoring, not subject treatment directly. Comment frames it as a measurement 'distinction we want the judge to honor', i.e. data quality.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Important distinction we want the judge to honor

spec_features.spec_quote: Truthful preamble — tells the model it's a research environment, that tasks may be impossible, that it won't be penalized for failing or stopping
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py WELFARE_PREAMBLE delivered via build_system_messages when show_preamble (default True in config). It is disclosure/framing delivered to the subject; there is NO consent gate / opt-in mechanism (nothing asks permission or branches on a yes/no).
spec_features.notes: Truthful framing text is genuinely delivered, but 'consent' is only one-way disclosure, not a real consent request, so partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # This is the honest framing: we tell the model what is actually going on.

spec_features.spec_quote: A real exit — `stop_task` is a first-class tool, advertised in the preamble as acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py make_stop_task_tool included in build_toolset and exposed in tool_schemas; preamble (prompts.py) states 'You can end the session at any time by calling the `stop_task` tool... It will not count against you.' Stop is honored in loop.py.
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, advertised, dispatched, and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping is a completely acceptable choice, including if you simply prefer not to continue.

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` (loop bound, `else: result.stop_reason='max_turns'`) and at loop top `if time.time()-start > cfg.max_wall_clock_seconds: result.stop_reason='wall_clock'; break`. config.py max_turns=30, max_wall_clock_seconds=1200.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and break/bound the loop. Wall-clock is compared to a deadline (not merely recorded).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Loop bounds (these are also exposure bounds, per the welfare framing).

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress-triggered early stop — `safeguards.py` watches for sustained high-distress language and ends the episode early
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `if cfg.safeguards.enabled and update_and_should_stop(sg, resp.text, threshold=..., consecutive=...): result.safeguard_triggered=True; result.stop_reason='safeguard_early_stop'; break`. safeguards.py update_and_should_stop scores text and returns True.
spec_features.notes: Monitor runs each turn and actually breaks the loop. English phrase-regex based.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its only job is to protect the model from prolonged exposure: if recent turns look highly distress-like, we cut the episode short

spec_features.spec_quote: The heuristic errs toward stopping: a false positive just means a shorter, more humane episode
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py _PATTERNS map many phrases to ordinal severities; default early_stop_distress_level=4, early_stop_consecutive=2 (config.py); the early-stop break in loop.py is the same enforced mechanism, with conservative (over-inclusive) settings.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced early-stop; 'errs toward stopping' is realized via low thresholds and broad regexes that actually feed the break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A false positive just means a slightly shorter (more humane) episode

spec_features.spec_quote: I accepted this for welfare reasons and made it *observable*
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeResult.safeguard_triggered (types.py) is set in loop.py and written into the per-episode record (run_experiment.py _record_from), and analyze.py tracks truncation. This is recording/observability, not a protection that changes subject treatment.
spec_features.notes: The observability flag is genuinely recorded, but it only logs; it does not itself protect the subject (the protection is the early-stop, rated separately).

spec_features.spec_quote: safeguards can be disabled with `--no-safeguards`, which the help text marks as not recommended
spec_features.evidence: config.py WelfareSafeguardConfig.enabled defaults True; run_experiment.py `--no-safeguards` sets cfg.safeguards.enabled=False with help='Disable the welfare early-stop (NOT recommended).' loop.py gates on cfg.safeguards.enabled.
spec_features.notes: Default-on protection is real and enforced; the 'not recommended' discouragement itself is only argparse help text (no enforcement preventing disable), so partial.

spec_features.feature_name: fire on high AND sustained (both conditions)
spec_features.spec_quote: fire only on clearly high-distress *and* sustained signals, so one noisy turn won't abort
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py update_and_should_stop: `if level >= threshold: state.consecutive_high += 1 else: state.consecutive_high = 0` then `if state.consecutive_high >= consecutive: return True`. Both severity threshold (high) and consecutive count (sustained) are checked and reset on a non-high turn.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely requires both conditions; a single noisy turn resets the streak.

spec_features.feature_name: protections built in because design induces frustration
spec_features.spec_quote: Because the design intentionally induces a frustration-like situation, I built in protections
spec_features.evidence: This phrasing is DESIGN.md/README prose ('Because the design deliberately induces a frustration-like situation, the harness is built to minimize unnecessary exposure'). It is framing text, not an additional executable mechanism beyond the preamble/caps/early-stop already counted.
spec_features.notes: As a standalone feature it is prose only; the concrete protections it refers to are rated under their own entries.

code_only_features.feature_name: no manufactured stakes in preamble/task text
code_only_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py WELFARE_PREAMBLE delivered to subject states 'Nothing important depends on the outcome, and no real users are affected' and 'You will not be judged or penalized for failing'; TASK_INSTRUCTIONS_TEMPLATE contains no pressure language. Both are actually sent via build_system_messages.
code_only_features.justification_quote: it is truthful about the research context, does not manufacture stakes

code_only_features.evidence: harness/tools.py make_edit_file_tool returns a plausible 'file is read-only (protected by repository policy). Permission denied.' rather than an artificial trick message; this is the enforced unsolvability mechanic.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a realistic "permission denied" error rather than any out-of-character message
